selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveler first notice about the convictions of the enlightened minds?
questions.answer: He saw that, even though they differed in ability and approach, they shared the same belief in Allah’s oneness and held it with firmness.

questions.question: What is striking about those minds even before their agreement is mentioned?
questions.answer: They differ from one another in strength, approach, and way of thinking.

questions.question: How is the agreement of these minds described in relation to truth?
questions.answer: It is described as a strong chain and as a bright opening that gives access to the world of truth.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the durability of that truth?
questions.answer: It describes it as deeply rooted and impossible to tear away.

questions.question: How are those hearts described in their relationship to divine knowledge?
questions.answer: Each heart is presented as a place reflecting lordly knowledge and as a broad mirror showing need before Allah.

questions.question: How can the hearts agree if their methods are not the same?
questions.answer: They can agree because truth is one, even when people reach it through different ways.

questions.question: Why does the passage say their agreement is a trustworthy guide and teacher?
questions.answer: Because so many sincere and perceptive hearts and minds agreeing together makes their testimony dependable.

questions.question: What stronger image follows the window comparison?
questions.answer: The hearts together are compared to a vast mirror or a sea reflecting the sun.

questions.question: What two groups are presented in the summary statement at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Upright, illuminated minds and sound, luminous hearts.

questions.question: What short statement marks the traveler’s acceptance of this truth?
questions.answer: He says that he has believed in Allah.

questions.question: What main subject unites the whole target passage?
questions.answer: The whole passage centers on how both sound intellects and purified hearts point together to Allah’s necessary existence and oneness.

questions.question: How does the passage balance difference and unity among these intellects?
questions.answer: It says they differ in personal ability and thought, yet agree in faith and certainty.

questions.question: What does their unity in belief prove to the traveler?
questions.answer: It proves to him that they are resting on a single truth that does not change.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying their roots are deep?
questions.answer: It means their belief is established on a strong foundation.

questions.question: In what matter do those hearts fully agree?
questions.answer: They fully agree regarding Allah’s necessary existence and His unity.

questions.question: What do those hearts experience that supports faith?
questions.answer: They experience spiritual discovery and inward witnessing that agree with each other.

questions.question: What does the comparison to the sun help explain?
questions.answer: It helps explain that one truth can be reflected in many places without becoming many different truths.

questions.question: What does the passage communicate by gathering all those hearts into one large image?
questions.answer: It communicates that their combined witness is even stronger than their individual witness.

questions.question: How does the passage connect certainty with both reason and spirituality?
questions.answer: It presents intellect as reaching shared conviction and hearts as reaching matching spiritual insight, both leading to the same belief.

questions.question: What does the Arabic summary section restate in simple terms?
questions.answer: It restates that both enlightened minds and luminous hearts, though diverse in their ways, agree in pointing to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What did the traveler discover when he began examining enlightened intellects?
questions.answer: He discovered that they all held the same settled belief about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that some of their viewpoints even oppose others?
questions.answer: It highlights that their agreement in faith is powerful precisely because it remains despite serious differences.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the source of their confidence?
questions.answer: It suggests that their confidence comes from a deep and lasting reality.

questions.question: What two images are used to explain the consensus of the intellects?
questions.answer: It is compared to a strong chain and to a bright window opening onto truth.
